output.answer: Yes. Qualcomm announced a global, performance-focused workforce reduction in an October 19, 2026 memo, with notifications expected to begin in November; reporting on November 11 said layoffs had begun in India. Qualcomm has not disclosed the number of jobs to be eliminated globally or in India, and it did not confirm the reported India total.
caveats: The reported figure of more than 1,000 India jobs is an estimate and Qualcomm has not confirmed it.
The Form 10-K confirms severance-related restructuring charges but does not state how many employees were affected; the $332 million figure is not itself a headcount figure.

passages.quote: In an internal memo to employees on October 19, reviewed by Reuters, CEO Cristiano Amon described the exercise as a “performance-focused reduction” following the company’s annual employee reviews. Notifications to affected employees were expected to begin in November.

More than 1,000 jobs could be at risk in India as Qualcomm undertakes a global workforce reduction, although the U.S. chipmaker has not disclosed the number of positions likely to be eliminated in the country.
Other expenses in fiscal 2026 consisted of restructuring and restructuring-related charges (substantially all of which related to severance costs).

output.question: Has Qualcomm announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: CEO Cristiano Amon’s October 19, 2026 internal memo described a global “performance-focused reduction” following annual employee reviews, with notifications expected to begin in November.

The Hindu reported on November 11, 2026 that more than 1,000 Qualcomm India jobs could be at risk, while noting that Qualcomm had not disclosed the number of positions likely to be eliminated in India.
Qualcomm’s fiscal 2026 Form 10-K reported $332 million in restructuring and restructuring-related charges, substantially all related to severance costs.
